Here's a key detail about the new Apple Upgrade Program: "If you buy an iPhone with a lease, you must connect to AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon at signup."

In a new article today, John Gruber of Daring Fireball offers a plausible explanation for this requirement.

Apple Upgrade's iPhone Restrictions

According to a former Apple employee who was on Apple's carrier team and emailed Gruber, this requirement stems primarily from the agreements Apple has with US carriers Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile.

The contracts Apple negotiates with each carrier are worth "hundreds of millions of dollars," and Apple makes certain concessions in exchange for this funding. Requiring iPhones purchased through Apple Upgrade to be connected to a T-Mobile, Verizon, or AT&T account is one such concession.

The former Apple employee went on to explain more about these carrier agreements:

There's also a fraud and risk assessment aspect at play. Another former Apple Store retail employee told Gruber that once Apple began offering carrier installment plans in its retail stores, iPhone-related fraud "went through the roof."

Apple does note that while you need to connect your iPhone to AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon when you sign up for Apple Upgrade, the iPhone itself is not network-locked: "To get an iPhone with a lease, you must choose a qualifying carrier (but not a prepaid carrier plan). Leased iPhones are always unlocked, and you can switch carriers at any time, subject to the terms of your selected carrier."

You can read Gruber's full article at Daring Fireball.
